OD1.currentOperation: STBY waiting for BOUM-0001 location clearance, to start jack-down and move to BM-0001
OD1.nextSteps: Rig preparation for move; rig move for new well BOUM-0001

highlights: OD1 was idle for a second week, still waiting on BOUM-0001 location clearance to start jack-down. Last week activities are again recorded as Nil.
Overstay crew fell from 11 to 8. COSL came down from 11 to 7, and HLB now holds 1 where it held none.
OD1 personnel onboard eased from 79 to 78, and visa holders rose from 57 to 58.

CA1 took 300 m³ of fuel from the bunker barge MT SEDRA-II at Mina Al Ahmadi anchorage on Sat 12. The workbook records it as an adjustment to balance the 294.2 m³ given to OPH on 06 and 07 Sep, which settles where last week's fuel went.
Vessel movements were 23 against 18, the busiest of the four weeks tracked. Charlie-3 made 13 of them.
CA5 has now spent 14 straight days on station at OD1 without moving between locations, across both this week and last.
Truck and pickup moves held at 44, but turned outbound again: 25 out against 19 in, where the week before ran 12 out and 32 in as the BM-0001 casing arrived.

Casing went back out: 30", 24" and 36" and 38" R3 joints returned to KOC Ahmadi Yard 4 across Sat 12, Sun 13 and Mon 14, and 18-5/8" R3 went to HETCO for inspection and came back to the Shuaiba pipe yard.
Charlie-3 ran crew changes through two new transfer points, Jal Boot Village and Khiran Marina, alongside the usual Shuaiba runs.
dataNotes: Vessel sheet 11.09 has two CA1 rows and no CA3 row. The second (E9, fresh water 120 m³ to OPH) is CA3: CA1 was at OD1 that day, and CA3 had anchored at OPH the evening before. Read as CA3 here.

Vessel sheet 13.09 Charlie-3 repeats 11.09 word for word, including every timestamp: cast off 04:50, 500 m zone 05:55, alongside 06:00, departed 06:40, secured Shuaiba 07:55, same 7 Pax, same 1 lift discharged, same 3 lifts loaded. One of the two days is almost certainly a copied row. Both are counted as written. Confirm.

Port sheet 10.09: E11 and E12 are identical and share delivery ticket COSL-DT-OP-RI3-N-21-3C, so they are counted as one truck. E10 and E13 are also identical, and only one truck of 10 casing joints was dispatched to HETCO that day (E6), so they are counted as one.
Port sheet 14.09: E45 and E46 are identical and share delivery ticket 2026/9/14/1129, counted as one. Ticket HPM-DT-1583 is used twice, on E43 and E48, for different cargo.
Port sheet 15.09 E61 offloads two trucks of X-Overs and Landing Joints that have no arrival line anywhere in the sheet. Counted as two arrivals so they are not lost.
Bentonite, 23 MT on 14.09 for OD1: the Port sheet (E51) says it was pumped on CA3, the Vessel sheet (E20) says CA1 received it. Confirm which vessel carried it.
Two port-side locations are new this week, Jal Boot Village and Khiran Marina, both used for crew transfer by taxi boat. Neither is a rig, so runs to them are not counted as vessel movements.

CA1 on 11.09 came alongside CA5 in DP mode to collect a modified flange. Vessel to vessel, inside the OD1 field, so not counted as a movement. CA1 also ran a DP trial from Shuaiba on 16.09 and returned, which is not a rig call.
Port sheet E8 and E9 on 10.09 are one sentence split across two rows. The second row begins with a tab and no verb.
Reporting window is 7 days, the same as the previous report, so the counts are directly comparable for the first time in this series.
